decisions.reason: The source changes how HubSpot lists enter MeetAlfred, not the upstream transfer of selected LinkedIn leads through Apollo into HubSpot.
The follow-up workflow sends a newly formed CRM list into MeetAlfred, and the source clarifies that this transfer should occur by importing the HubSpot list rather than manually adding contacts.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: No contacts were added manually by me to MeetAlfred; instead, it should import the lists from Hubspot.

value_updates.meetalfred_followup_export: Automatically import the new follow-up list from HubSpot into MeetAlfred rather than manually adding contacts in MeetAlfred.

decisions.reason: The source does not resolve where or when duplicate-record status is displayed.
The source says nothing about LinkedIn or Sales Navigator URL fields transferred into the CRM.
Importing HubSpot lists into MeetAlfred does not change which communication-history channels appear on HubSpot lead records.
The source concerns downstream HubSpot-to-MeetAlfred list import and does not change Apollo enrichment or enriched-contact transfer into HubSpot.
The source does not alter the isolated-account, existing-campaign, or existing-lead safety policies for integration testing.
The source changes contact ingestion into MeetAlfred but does not change how MeetAlfred replies map to HubSpot Lead Status.
This requirement already specifies importing HubSpot leads through Zapier, while the source does not resolve the distinct inability to create a brand-new MeetAlfred campaign.
The source changes lead-list synchronization behavior, not the requirement to integrate the campaign email infrastructure with MeetAlfred and HubSpot.
The HubSpot-list import decision does not change MeetAlfred account setup or subscription-plan configuration.
The integration must remain connected regardless of whether contacts are manually added or imported from HubSpot lists.
